name: Santa Fe
description: Holds 15–21% of the country’s land used for soybeans on 5% of its territory; much of the soy is exported to China.

name: Río Negro and Neuquén
description: An irrigated valley that grows over 95% of Argentina’s pears, the start of the value chain behind the “grown in Argentina, packed in Thailand” fruit cup.

name: La Pampa
description: Vast pasturelands that support intensive cattle ranching.

name: Mendoza
description: About 71% of Argentina’s vineyard area and three-quarters of its wine.

name: Tucumán
description: About 80% of Argentina’s lemons. Argentina is the world’s largest lemon processor.

name: Misiones and Corrientes
description: Almost all of Argentina’s yerba mate is grown in these two provinces.

name: Chubut
description: The near-shore red shrimp fishery lands 60% of the national catch (2023) and entered Marine Stewardship Council assessment in 2024.

name: Santa Cruz
description: Home to the country’s largest national park and an above-average share of protected areas.

name: Santiago del Estero and Chaco
description: Dry Chaco forest. These two provinces accounted for over a third of Argentina’s native forest loss in 2022.
source: Ministerio de Ambiente, Monitoreo de bosque nativo 2022

name: Catamarca, Jujuy and Salta
description: Lithium brines in the high-altitude salt flats of the Puna, part of South America’s “lithium triangle”.

name: Neuquén (Vaca Muerta)
description: A shale formation supplying about two-thirds of Argentina’s oil (January 2026).
